questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hand ready on both the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand ready on both the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has only one brake light, which is not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers see that you are slowing down faster than they may expect.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: The suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the weight you are carrying.

questions.question: Which item will NOT help you avoid serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: What should you do to make yourself more visible?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on all the time.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothes, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Block your view of road hazards.
Invite other riders to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. Never stay in another driver's blind spot for a long time.

questions.question: After entering a turn, what should you do with the throttle?

options.text: Keep steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through the turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: How should you ride in a group to stay close while keeping safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets you stay close while keeping enough space between riders for safety. Use single-file when going around curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: Which is NOT needed for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: Being too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
Allowing clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to flow to prevent fogging, and fit with room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You rarely hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are usually:

options.text: More powerful than a car's headlights.
Just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Not as powerful as a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to stay comfortable in the wind and cold.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay comfortable in the wind and cold.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a rest break every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine—they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean as you lean. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which is NOT important?
questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have conflicts with other traffic?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other traffic is at intersections. Be extra alert at intersections where another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle:

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during daylight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly beside another vehicle. The driver may not see you and could enter your lane. Also, riding alongside blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect riding if you also drink alcohol.
Have the same effect on everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make riding more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal) have side effects that can impair your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percentage of a motorcycle's total braking power?
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A good rain suit:

options.text: Is not needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not balloon when riding.
questions.explanation: A good motorcycle rain suit will not tear or balloon up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Cut their space cushions in half.
Keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space between each rider for safety.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, you should do any of the following except:

options.text: Find a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with other activities.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Let your friend ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your friend ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Instead, find them a safe ride home, keep them busy with other activities, and prevent them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the driver.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when turning. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Stay in the right part of the lane.
Stay in the left part of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Not use your signal so you don't distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the left part of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane. Use your signal, check for traffic, and pass when it is safe. Signal again before returning to your original lane.

questions.question: In a crash, you can reduce serious injury by doing all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury risk when riding.
